claims.claim: In the exact inline d/sigma=3/8, L/sigma=1/8 configuration, nonoverlap of two rigid equal spheres requires sigma>16R/3
claims.limitations: A geometry fact; no preparation, shielding, material or electrodynamics claim; sigma=R is impossible in this exact setup.

claims.claim: Uniform solid spheres convolved with the same Gaussian preserve negative DP initial-PPT slope for tested non-overlapping R/sigma values
claims.limitations: Same static H=0, rigid COM branches, Gaussian kernel; omits mechanical and environmental dynamics; not a new general DP viability result.

claims.claim: For an ideal zero-thickness Faraday shield at the closest surface gap, Q=2L/(d-2R)>2/3 for the exact example
claims.limitations: Faraday shield necessity and qualitative Q<<1 are paper arguments, not absolute no-go or measured decoherence; actual screen/dipole noise not calculated.

claims.claim: For the particular Gaussian softened point-pair potential, F/FN is ~0.004855 at the minimum branch centre gap and ~0.011323 at mean separation
claims.limitations: Not an experiment-specific inverse-square-law exclusion; torsion-balance convolution/uncertainties required.

claims.claim: XENONnT 2026 reports R0>4.5e-10 m at 95% CL for its specified Markovian DP model; this alone does not exclude illustrative sigma of micrometres
claims.limitations: Requires mapping Gaussian sigma and nuclear/electronic assumptions; upper bound in S27 is conditional macroscopic-classicality criterion.

claims.claim: Single-body Gaussian DP heating scales as G*hbar*m/(4*sqrt(pi)*sigma^3), so micrometre sigma gives tiny intrinsic heating in the point-mass formula
claims.limitations: Not full many-constituent noise or thermal decoherence, no claim experiment viable.
